description: This course explores blockchain technology's role in enhancing cybersecurity through cryptographic foundations, consensus algorithms, and decentralized identity management. Topics include cryptographic hashing (SHA-256), public-key cryptography (RSA, ECC), and zero-knowledge proofs (zk-SNARKs); blockchain architecture (Hyperledger Fabric, Ethereum) and consensus mechanisms (Proof of Work, Proof of Stake); secure smart contracts (Solidity, Truffle) and their vulnerabilities; decentralized identity frameworks (DIDs, Verifiable Credentials); and blockchain-based threat detection systems (blockchain forensics, immutable audit trails). The course also covers standards like ISO/IEC 20248 for digital identity and NIST guidelines for blockchain security.

clos.text: Define cryptographic hashing algorithms (SHA-256) and their role in blockchain immutability.
Describe the architecture of Hyperledger Fabric and Ethereum blockchains in cybersecurity contexts.
Explain zero-knowledge proofs (zk-SNARKs) and their application in privacy-preserving authentication.
Apply smart contract security principles to detect and mitigate vulnerabilities in Solidity code.
Implement a decentralized identity system using Verifiable Credentials and DID protocols.
